 Samsung Electronics and Apple reduce their OLED panel orders, and Samsung Display may see weaker Q4 profit
 Samsung Electronics and Apple reduce their OLED panel orders, and Samsung Display may see weaker Q4 profit 
 Share on LinkedIn 
 Samsung Display may see weaker results in the fourth quarter of 2026, as its two largest customers, Apple and Samsung Electronics, are reportedly scaling back their smartphone component orders following the sharp rise in memory prices. According to industry sources, Samsung's mobile division asked its suppliers to reduce their Q4 component deliveries by 20-30% from earlier plans, while Apple cut its October orders for certain iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max parts by 15-20%.
 The cuts come at a time of year when new flagship launches usually boost orders for high-end OLED panels. Samsung Electronics normally reduces its handset production ahead of each new Galaxy S launch, but the latest reported cuts are steeper than expected. And Samsung Display is highly exposed to these two customers - according to its 2025 audited accounts, Apple and Samsung Electronics generated 40.4% and 22.4% of its annual revenue, respectively. Together, these two customers accounted for around $14.1 billion, or 62.8% of the company's sales.
   Lower premium OLED orders could hurt Samsung Display's profits more than the shipment volumes suggest, as lower fab utilization raises the fixed costs per panel, and fewer high-margin panels drag down the product mix.
